goals.g1: Is there a hybrid subtraction design that improves on the current 4-phase mechanism under BOTH constraints: layer economy AND rule-authoring rigor?

s_layer_cost.statement: One ruleset firing produces exactly one persisted layer; deferring work into extra layers explodes the floor count, catastrophic at bitwise density (KB layer_model).

s_layer_cost_unquantified.statement: The real cost of a layer is unquantifiable until the GA is realized (user, this session); layer counts are a relative ordering criterion, not an absolute budget.

s_locality.statement: Rules match exact local subgraphs; no node can locally know global facts such as being above the lowest 1-bit or the eventual sign.

s_counts.statement: Firing-count model swept over 0..31 squared plus 2000 random 16-bit pairs: 4-phase avg 18.68, naive full-negate hybrid 19.15, Arm-transit 25.06; skewed case 1-1000000: 21 vs 40 vs 60.

s_table_provenance.statement: The frontier table was brute-forced from ground truth after hand-encodings failed; 2 of 8 keys were asserted, not proven, unreachable (KB VALIDATED_MECHANISM_2026_07_05).

a_subdef.statement: Standard full-subtractor recurrence defines per-bit subtraction.
a_subdef.negation_note: standard full-subtractor recurrence; flips only if Perspective's bit convention differs from LSB-first/this formula — still unverified against engine source

d_lower_bound.statement: Under locality, any negative-path design must walk the low bits twice: once computing a-b (sign unknowable before the frontier) and once rewriting to b-a (correction must propagate node by node). Sequential-firing lower bound is about 2*len(a) + overhang; the 4-phase achieves it, clean-pass designs pay the overhang twice.

derived_from.rule: the two walks are information-theoretically forced by late sign discovery plus local-only propagation; the count model confirms 4-phase sits at the bound and full-width negate exceeds it by the overhang length

d_table_derived.statement: The frontier table is not arbitrary: it is exactly a full subtractor at the frontier column with minuend right_here, subtrahend 1 (the left MSB), and borrow_in = NOT(b1) AND b2. All 6 table entries match the formula.

derived_from.rule: phase-2 output equals the low bits of b-a; the true b-a borrow into the frontier is 1 iff b_low < a_low iff (R>0 AND b1=0); b2 encodes R>0; substituting gives the formula, verified against all 6 brute-forced entries

d_unreachable_proved.statement: Keys (1,1,0) and (0,1,0) are provably unreachable, not just unobserved: a borrow's first appearance in phase 1 always sets that diff bit to 1 (exhaustive 4-case bit check), so b1=1 implies R>0, which implies b2=1. Confirmed by 1,046,529-pair sweep with zero occurrences.

derived_from.rule: case analysis on the full-subtractor recurrence at the first borrow-producing position, plus exhaustive empirical sweep

ans.statement: Adopt the epistemic hybrid: 4-phase mechanism and layer structure unchanged; frontier table content now DERIVED (frontier = full subtractor with borrow_in = NOT(b1) AND b2) and the 6-key coverage now PROVEN sufficient (b1=1 implies b2=1). Structural hybrids are rejected on the layer obligation.

derived_from.rule: the layer obligation eliminates both structural candidates; the derivation and proof close exactly the two rigor gaps the 4-phase had, at zero structural cost

h_struct.statement: Structural hybrid: replace phases 2-3 with a full-width uniform negate
h_struct.discriminator: Simplest rules, but pays the overhang walk twice — fails the layer obligation under skew.

h_dual.statement: Dual-track hybrid: compute a-b and b-a bits simultaneously per phase-1 firing, discard the losing track at the frontier
h_dual.discriminator: Avoids a separate negate pass, but the discard signal must itself propagate node-by-node (locality), costing the same second walk while roughly quadrupling rule variants.

h_epistemic.statement: Epistemic hybrid: keep the 4-phase layer structure byte-for-byte; replace the brute-forced frontier table with the derived borrow_in=NOT(b1) AND b2 full-subtractor formula, and the asserted unreachability with the proof
h_epistemic.discriminator: Zero layer-count change; upgrades the design's weakest epistemic component from brute-forced+asserted to derived+proven; changes no graph structure.

k_struct.result: 1-1000000: 40 firings vs 21 for 4-phase; overhang re-walked; fails ob_layers

k_dual.method: locality analysis of the discard signal
k_dual.result: winner signal must propagate per node = same second walk as phase 2, with ~4x rule variants and losing-track garbage to clean; no layer saving, higher rule cost

k_epist.method: formula vs table + unreachability sweep + exhaustive bit-level case check
k_epist.result: all 6 table entries match the derived formula; 1,046,529-pair sweep found zero (b1=1,b2=0) states; 4-case exhaustive check confirms a borrow's first appearance forces diff=1

k_ob_layers.result: identical to 4-phase by construction — no structural change

k_ob_rigor.result: table now derived from the recurrence; unreachability now proven; no brute-forced-only content remains in the mechanism spec

k_ans.method: searched the swept input space (0..31 squared + 2000 random 16-bit pairs) for ANY case where a structural candidate uses FEWER firings than 4-phase
k_ans.result: full-negate beats 4-phase only on near-equal-length negatives by at most 1 firing (e.g. 2-3: 5 vs 6; 8-9: 11 vs 12) while losing by up to 19 under skew; no regime where a structural hybrid dominates; rejection stands

obligations.ob_layers: Any adopted design must not exceed the 4-phase's sequential firing count materially, especially under operand-length skew.
obligations.ob_rigor: Any adopted design must not rest on brute-forced-only rule content or unproven reachability assertions.

committed.statement: Adopt the epistemic hybrid: 4-phase mechanism and layer structure unchanged; frontier table content now DERIVED (frontier = full subtractor with borrow_in = NOT(b1) AND b2) and the 6-key coverage now PROVEN sufficient (b1=1 implies b2=1). Structural hybrids are rejected on the layer obligation.
